Hi Samira / Jason,

Great speaking on Thursday — thanks for outlining Oakridge's short-term pilot goals and the 12–18 month performance roadmap. Per our conversation, attached is a short set of three dedicated reservation options designed to align cost, latency SLOs, and staged activation windows. The attachment is a compact proposal (see oakridge_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf) but I summarized the options inline to make review quicker.

TL;DR — three pathways depending on initial throughput and desired runway:
- Option A: Baseline Sprint — 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool), min guarantee 2 GPUs. Ramp: prewarm week (1 GPU steady), move to 20% traffic week 2, full pilot at week 4.
- Option B: Growth Lane — 24 x GPUs, min guarantee 8. Ramp: 2-week prewarm (KV warming + prefix caching), slow traffic ramp over 6 weeks (20% / 50% / 80% / 100%). Includes burst allowance + 25% ephemeral capacity for seasonal spikes.
- Option C: Enterprise Slate — 64 x GPUs, min guarantee 24 (staggered activation). Designed for model ensembles and stress testing; 8-week staged onramp with canary routing and automatic fallbacks to quantized variants.

Notes: each option includes suggestions for batching/KV cache warm-up, recommended model variants (fp16 vs 4-bit quantized), and an estimate of token-cost per hour under typical batch distributions. Region assumed: us-east1 (we can shift to another region if you prefer).

Next steps: if any of these map to your internal sizing, I can loop Karthik for technical footprint validation and Ben for commercial terms (12-month commit discounts, SLA). Would you prefer a short 30-min review early next week?

Attachments: oakridge_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf (pdf, 312KB)

Hi Samira / Marissa — quick technical supplement to clarify latency, warm-up, and min-GPU semantics.

1) Min guarantee semantics: the "min GPUs" in the proposal refers to reservation capacity that is pinned to your account in a region. If you require a geo-redundant standby that counts toward the min, we can split reservations across regions but that will change pricing and activation windows.

2) Latency 99p estimate: for a 4-shot 512-token average prompt on the Growth Lane (24 GPUs) assuming continuous batching target of 8ms accumulation window and optimized kernel selection: 99p ≈ 260–330ms. If you use a larger batched push (aggressive batching to save cost) you might see higher tail latencies — we recommend the 8ms window for production web endpoints.

3) Warm-up strategy: recommend 10–14 days of progressive prefix/KV prefill. Practical recipe: 
   - Days 0–3: controlled KV writes + replay a synthetic prompt set (50% of peak QPS)
   - Days 4–7: ramp to 30% live traffic; enable prefix caching and monitor cache hit ratio
   - Days 8–14: move to 60–100% traffic over rolling canaries; enable burst windows for stress tests

4) Minimum shard sizing & model variants: for the Growth Lane we recommend a shard size of 6 GPUs per serving shard (4 shards across 24 GPUs) to balance KV memory and throughput. This lets you run fp16 for latency-critical models and switch to 4-bit quantized variants for cost tiering on non-critical routes.

5) Fallback & graceful degradation: our smart routing policy can route to quantized variants or lower-cost regions when load exceeds reserved capacity. We can bake an automatic fallback policy into the rollout config so your front-end sees degraded throughput rather than full failures.

Attachment: oakridge_tech_footprint.xlsx (sheet includes shard sizing, expected GPU-memory utilization, and suggested warm-up sequences).

Happy to review these in the Tue 10am PT call.

— Karthik
